summary: 2.13x over amdclang (240 pairs, CI 2.125 to 2.139; 0.108 ms -> 0.051 ms), verified on the full battery (98 cases). Source-level restructure plus a one-instruction machine edit: one wave (block 16x4) handles 4 positions x 4 heads; powf/sincosf are computed once per (position, lane) and reused for 4 heads instead of once per head, and because elements e and e+64 share the angle (rotary_dim == 128) each lane loads both halves once and writes both outputs, so the input is read once instead of twice; all 8 x4 loads are issued before the stores. Case: the baseline was arithmetic-bound (reference headroom 2.27, 1186 VALU per thread for 16 bytes) and also read q/k twice; the result sits at headroom 1.06 of the copy model, i.e. now memory-bound. Caveats: outputs meet the manifest tolerance (same formulas, FMA contraction may differ), not guaranteed bit-identical; the rotary_dim != 128 fallback path (baseline's per-vector rule) is compiled in but is not exercised by the battery, which always passes 128.

friction: static_check error on amdclang's own output (state 8d444021566c1e66, .Lft21[162] `v_mad_u64_u32 v[8:9], s[0:1], s13, v8, v[54:55]`: 'reads v55, which is never written'). The high half of the addend only feeds the result's high half v9, which is discarded (only v8 is copied out, v[8:9] is overwritten at [167]). It is amdclang's idiom for a 64x32 multiply's upper partial product. The same pattern is only a warning when the register is written on some path (a9d3449b650245d7: v37, v21, v45). A dead-result-half analysis, or an automatic 'define with 0' fixup pass, would avoid the hand edit.

source() requires the full text on every call even when only `defines` and the launch change; a `source(parent=<state>, defines=..., launch=...)` form that reuses the stored text (the sha was identical: 9fcd23113d6987b8) would make sweeps cheap.

No battery case varies rotary_dim (fixed at 128 in the manifest), so the general-rotary_dim fallback path of a restructured kernel cannot be verified; nor is the in-place case (q == q_rope) that the source comment allows.
list_states does not show the coarsen factor of earlier states; the action params had to be guessed.
lessons: fi_rope: baseline spends ~1186 VALU instructions per thread (4 powf + 4 sincosf) to move 16 bytes, reference headroom 2.27. Computing the per-position trig once and reusing it for several heads in the same wave gave 2.13x and brought headroom to 1.06. When a kernel recomputes a wave-invariant-per-row expensive function for every output row/head, group the heads into one workgroup at source level first.

Heads per workgroup 4 vs 8 (trig amortized over 4 or 8 heads, 8 or 16 x4 loads in flight): 2.11x vs 2.09x at 60 pairs, i.e. equal; once at headroom ~1.08 the amortization factor no longer matters. HG=8 needed 96 VGPRs (occupancy 5 waves/SIMD, limiter vgpr) with no measurable penalty versus 56 VGPRs.
Block 16x4 (one wave per workgroup) vs 16x16 (4 waves): 2.133 vs 2.133, no difference for a loop-free memory-bound body.

RoPE non-interleaved with rotary_dim == head_dim: elements e and e + rd/2 share the angle, so one lane can load both halves once and write both outputs (32 bytes per lane read, 32 written) instead of the baseline's two loads per 16-byte store; loads-before-stores is also safe for the in-place case.

amdclang emits v_mad_u64_u32 with an addend pair whose high half is never written when only the low 32 bits of the result are used; static_check rejects it as an error. Fix: insert `v_mov_b32_e32 vN, 0` before it (one instruction, no timing effect).

session.final:
`fi_rope` is now **2.13x** faster than amdclang's build (0.108 ms → 0.051 ms, 240 pairs, CI 2.125–2.139). The shipped state is `d2cff034e937d07f`; it passes the static check and the full 98-case battery, and the report is recorded.

- **Which case this was:** the baseline was arithmetic-bound, not memory-bound (reference headroom 2.27). Each thread ran about 1,186 arithmetic instructions (4 `powf` + 4 `sincosf`) to move 16 bytes, and it read each input twice.
- **What changed (source level):**
  - One wave now handles 4 positions × 4 heads, so the trig is computed once per position and lane and reused across those heads.
  - Elements `e` and `e+64` share an angle when `rotary_dim == 128`, so each lane loads both halves once and writes both outputs.
  - All loads are issued before the stores.
- **Machine edit:** amdclang's output for this variant failed the static check on a read of a never-written register (`v55`). I added one `v_mov_b32_e32 v55, 0`; the affected result half is discarded, so it changes nothing else.
- **Where it stands:** headroom is now 1.06 against the copy model, so the kernel is memory-bound. Eight heads per workgroup (2.09x) and a 16×16 block (2.13x) were indistinguishable from the shipped state, so I stopped there after about five timed candidates.

Caveats:
- Outputs meet the manifest tolerance but are not guaranteed bit-identical to the baseline.
- The fallback path for `rotary_dim != 128` is compiled in but never exercised, because the battery always passes 128.
- The in-place case (`q == q_rope`) is also not covered by the battery.

Friction logged in the report: the static-check error on amdclang's own multiply idiom, and `source()` needing the full text resent for a defines-only sweep.
